title: Elastic Cycle Quotas: Decision Framework for Temporary Shore-Up and Graceful Feature Throttle
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Define and pilot an operational framework that lets PMs and ENG managers allocate a small, elastic reserve of staffing and scope credits that can be drawn down mid-cycle to respond to high-priority incidents, unexpected infra work, or tactical opportunities while minimizing overall scope churn. The framework combines quantitative signals (burn rate, cycle WIP, active incidents, latency/cost regressions) with qualitative approvals and automated scope-throttle policies.

Why this ticket: We repeatedly face mid-cycle emergencies that force disruptive scope reshuffles and context-switching. Existing surge lanes are ad-hoc (Slack pings + triage meetings) and cause uneven product velocity across teams. The objective is to reduce cross-team overhead, make trade-offs transparent, and provide predictable guardrails (who can seed reserve, approval steps, and automated fallbacks).

Core components: 
- Reserve Credits: small pool of FTE-equivalent credits (e.g., 0.2 - 0.5 of a full-time engineer per micro-lane) that PMs can request to shore-up critical work without stealing from other teams. Credits are time-boxed and reconciled at cycle-end.
- Priority Lanes: three lanes (Urgent Incident, Customer Escalation, Strategic Burst). Each lane has pre-defined eligibility, SLA, approval path, and allowed duration.
- Soft-Cut Policy: a three-stage scope throttle (defer, reduce, swap) applied at ticket level; each stage has automated notifications and required reviewers.
- Triggers & Signals: automatic triggers from Observability (SLO breach >5% for 30m), cycle burn-rate >120% of plan, >2 P1 incidents in 72h, or a named customer escalations dashboard entry.
- Approval Flow: automated request form (Confluence -> GitHub issue template) + 48h auto-escalation to director if no decision.
- Audit & Reconciliation: cycle-end report (Console dashboard + Confluence summary) listing credits used, outcomes, and scope cuts.

Non-goals: This is not a replacement for long-term headcount planning or formal reductions to roadmap commitments across multi-cycle initiatives. It is specifically for short-term, controlled capacity reallocation inside a single cycle.

Success metrics: fewer unplanned scope deletions, reduced context-switching incidents, cycle predictability improvement (measured via Cycle Completion %, mean time to restore priority work), and qualitative PM/Eng satisfaction in pilot teams.
updates: 2026-03-05 - Ticket created by Priya Nair. Initial problem statement and high-level components drafted.

2026-03-06 - Sync with Eng Managers (Liam Chen, Maria Gomez). Agreed on three priority lanes and reserve credit range. Action: ENG to prototype automated trigger hooks from Console SLO alerts. (Owner: Liam)
2026-03-07 - Design input from Design (Aisha Kapoor) requested for simple request form UI in Console. Action: DES to deliver wireframes by 2026-03-11.

2026-03-09 - Trade-off discussion: if reserve credits are too large they mask chronic underplanning; decided to cap per-team draw at 0.5 FTE equivalent per cycle. Noted potential for gaming; added reconciliation and review steps.
2026-03-10 - PMs asked for ability to 'pre-reserve' credits for anticipated trade shows/releases; decision: allowed but flagged differently in audit report and subject to stricter approval.

2026-03-11 - ENG spike: prototype pipeline for auto-trigger: SLO breach -> create 'Reserve Request' draft in GH issues via API. Initial PR: github.com/redwood-inference/proc-automation/pull/489 (feedback: add rate limit to avoid noise).

2026-03-12 - Planning: pilot cohort selected (Search Ranking & Stream team). Pilot kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-16, 60-day evaluation. Documentation draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CycleElasticQuotas (internal), request form template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-templates/blob/main/reserve-request.md
acceptance_criteria: A working request flow exists (Console button + form) that creates a tracked issue with lane, rationale, requested credits, and TTL.
Automated triggers from Console SLO/dashboard fire a draft request with correct metadata in at least one pilot team.
Cycle-end audit report automatically aggregates reserve credit usage, decisions, and outcomes, published to Confluence.
Pilot teams (2) report >=20% reduction in mid-cycle scope deletions compared to previous quarter in initial 60-day run, or provide qualitative justification for adjustments.
Playbook document published with clear eligibility, approval flows, and reconciliation steps; PMs and Eng managers trained (recording available).
